memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Israel saw the sons of Joseph, he asked, 'Who are these?' 'They are the sons God has given me here,' Joseph said to his father. Then Israel said, 'Bring them to me so I may bless them.'" — Gen 48:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob's eyesight is failing, so he asks who the young men are. And Joseph's answer is worth pausing over: "They are the sons God has given me here."

He does not say "my sons" or "the ones born to me in Egypt." He says God gave them — and he says here, in the land of his slavery, his imprisonment and his exile. Joseph is able to look at the country that cost him twenty years and see it as a place where God gave him good gifts.

That is not denial. Joseph never pretends Egypt was easy. It is something harder and better: the ability to receive God's goodness in a place you did not choose.

Then Jacob says, "Bring them to me so I may bless them." He wants them close. And it is impossible to read that without hearing another voice saying something very similar: "Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them" (Matt 19:14). Jesus took children in His arms and blessed them.

Bring them to me. That is the heart of God towards the young — and towards you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you name a good gift God gave you in a season you would not have chosen?
2. Are there children or young people you should be bringing into the presence of God's people?
3. Do you believe Jesus genuinely wants you brought near, not kept at a distance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the good gifts You have given me even in hard places. Help me bring the young people in my life to You, and let me come close myself. Amen.
